rv.q: Everything matches and echoes everything else in this interpretation from Mr. Grindley (who directed the Tony-winning revival of “Journey’s End”), but in ways that creep up on you.

Does the Gentleman Caller with the sketchy past really love her or is he hunting fortunes? Does Eva really want the best for her fragile only daughter or is the manipulation more ominous? Any relation between this triangle and the one in "Glass Menagerie" is obvious but beside the point.
